MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L22·N8481unmasked layer
Mostly a low-magnitude, position-based neuron: it peaks on the function/head word that opens a new phrase-continuation right after a lead-in (e.g. "realize **that**", "try to **choose**", "created **an**", "serums **and**", "the **rest** of us"), and is strongly *suppressed* on tokens that complete a verbatim repeat of an earlier phrase ("contact **us**", "as a coach**?**", "**PH**A", "stands **for**").

This neuron has almost no coherent positive trigger — its top "activations" are weak, arbitrary mid-sentence tokens in descriptive third-person prose (a German review adjective, "th", a comma, " in", " loves", " The") — while its real signal is strongly negative: it is heavily suppressed by function words inside second-person promotional/how-to web copy ("you can easily browse…", "This will allow you…"), so it behaves as a suppression unit for marketing/instructional "you can" phrasing rather than a detector.
